basics.name: Nicholas Mastracola
basics.title: Software Developer & Systems Specialist
basics.summary: Technical professional with six years of client-facing implementation and automation experience (Node.js, SQL, API integration, browser automation) in EdTech, now applying the same problem-solving approach to inventory and operations systems in manufacturing while completing a B.S. in Computer Science. Comfortable moving between technical and operational domains — from reverse-engineering undocumented APIs to owning inventory accuracy for a 700+ employee facility.

highlights: Joined in production roles (Machine Operator; Pre-Trim/Whizzard operator) before moving into Parts Room Attendant in March 2026; LOTO (Lockout/Tagout) certified
Manage inventory across 4,000+ SAP material records supporting maintenance and production operations across ~15 production lines in a 700+ employee facility
Analyzed cycle count compliance and inventory accuracy issues; redesigned count scheduling and review processes in collaboration with planners and supervisors
Used SAP transaction data, Excel, and Power Query to analyze consumption trends, supplier lead times, and critical spare availability, supporting purchasing and shutdown-planning decisions
Defined requirements and evaluated Microsoft 365 tooling for a digital maintenance parts-request workflow, replacing an ad hoc manual process
Architected and built a centralized storeroom knowledge base covering procedures, vendor information, and SAP reference material for training and knowledge retention
Built a proof-of-concept Power BI dashboard for inventory metrics
Delivered LMS/Canvas migration projects for higher-ed and K-12 clients over six years, functioning as de facto technical lead across 5-10 concurrent migrations (peak 10-15)

Became the team's specialist for non-standard, undocumented-API migrations — reverse-engineered authentication and network traffic to export client data from LMS platforms with no supported API, covering 20+ clients across Blackboard, Schoology, and PowerSchool

Rebuilt and owned an internal Node.js/Postgres video migration tool for Canvas Studio, adding session-refresh handling for long-running jobs and an auditable record of migrated content; ownership required a formal handoff to another team upon departure
Directly influenced shipped Canvas Studio product decisions through ongoing collaboration with the Studio Product Manager
Wrote custom Node.js, SQL, and shell scripts, and used Puppeteer browser automation, to meet client-specific migration requirements without vendor API support
